A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AndroidWorld benchmark and M3A study. Their complete text, figures, tables, code listings and appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization and additions.

before.justification: V3 reports original M3A and SeeAct evaluations, human performance, error analyses and task-parameter robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 reports original agent evaluations and robustness results, including additional M3A-Simple and Gemma 2 experiments, three-seed results and an alternate device/OS test.

M1.justification: Section 4.1.1 introduces M3A-Simple, a variant using minimal prompting without guidelines or reflection. The full M3A action-generation/reflection loop and the SeeAct adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain 116 AndroidWorld tasks across 20 apps and the same 62-task MobileMiniWoB++ evaluation subset. V4 adds a Pixel 5/Android 12 test scenario alongside Pixel 6/Android 13. Appendix F documents existing tasks rather than establishing additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds M3A-Simple as an evaluated comparison agent using GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Gemma 2. The human and SeeAct comparators remain; the additional Gemma-backed full M3A is a model configuration of the existing method.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Gemma 2 27B, a control removing guidelines and reflection, and an alternate device/OS configuration. The existing seed-30 success-rate evaluation is retained. Temperature zero and explicit step-budget rules are newly disclosed, without evidence that settings of retained experiments changed.

E4.justification: V4 substantially extends analysis with the M3A-Simple prompting ablation, benchmark-level seed variation and an alternate device/OS robustness test. Appendix E.5 and Figure 8 add parameter-specific failure cases involving hidden expense categories and note-edit variants. The original five-task seed analysis and earlier error cases remain.

E5.justification: Section 5 newly reports results across three seeds and their mean, and discloses 20 trials per task for the retained five-task analysis. Figure 3 already provided 95% Wilson confidence intervals and significance annotations in v3 and is unchanged; no increase in its trial count is established.

E6.justification: All retained Table 3 scores are unchanged, but substantial new results are added. AndroidWorld/MobileMiniWoB++ percentages are 3.4/35.5, 14.7/55.2 and 19.8/67.7 for M3A-Simple with Gemma, Gemini and GPT-4 respectively, and 9.5/45.6 for full M3A with Gemma. Section 5 adds seed results of 27.6%, 26.3% and 33.2% (mean 29.0%), plus 28.4% on the alternate device/OS. These are additional conditions, not improvements to the retained scores.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a theorem or proof contribution. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised; the new material is experimental or documentary.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement and conclusion retain the dynamic 116-task, 20-app benchmark, M3A baseline, 30.6% headline success rate and importance of task-parameter robustness. Added experiments support these existing central claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of the prompting ablation, a qualified model-size explanation for Gemma's performance, and mechanisms linking seed sensitivity to hidden expense categories and note-edit complexity. The alternate-OS interpretation is explicitly limited to the tested case. The earlier limitations remain, condensed in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Appendix F substantially extends v3's selected examples with task templates, validation methods, associated apps and explicit per-task step limits with a human-derived rationale. V4 also specifies inference temperature, the 15:34 UTC clock reset and the supplementary API code location. Listing 1 omits the previously listed DOUBLE_TAP and SWIPE entries while scrolling remains documented. These documentation changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V4 adds AgentStudio to Section 2.1 and Table 1, adds Ferret-UI and Gemma 2 citations, and removes the AgentGPT and WebLlama references. The central positioning relative to AndroidEnv, OSWorld and MiniWoB++ remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Robustness moves from Section 4.4 into an expanded Section 5, limitations move to Appendix A, and the action-space explanation is reorganized. Headings, citation style and selected paragraphs are edited, without a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V4 adds a substantial task-catalog table in Appendix F and the expense-interface Figure 8. Table 3 is expanded and regrouped into comparison-agent, simplified-agent and full-agent blocks, while Table 1 gains AgentStudio. Existing Figures 1–7 are retained within a restyled and reflowed document.

improvement.justification: The new prompting control, open-model evaluation, seed results and device/OS check strengthen empirical support, while explicit task budgets improve reproducibility. These usefully refine an already supported benchmark. Benefits are tempered by the retained single-seed main comparisons and inconsistencies in the new catalog, such as minimum-brightness tasks instructing maximum brightness.
